title: A five-strip covering certificate for planar null geodesics in an equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou spacetime

scope.return: first strictly positive upward return before departure from int(D)
scope.D: r_+>=1/5, r_->=1/5, x^2+z^2<=64; all certified segments satisfy strict interior inequalities
scope.data: finite decimal box coordinates are exact rationals; strip endpoints are exact rationals

claims.claim: The exact affine charts are nonsingular and the five closed source strips are pairwise disjoint.
The first upward return exists on every closed source strip, remains in int(D), and is transverse; the return map is continuous on each closed strip.
claims.basis: two interval validations plus smooth ODE dependence and the implicit-function theorem in prose

claims.claim: K_OO covers N_O, K_OA covers N_A, K_AB covers N_B, K_BO covers N_O, and K_BA covers N_A. Each also covers every listed successor strip in its target box.
claims.basis: all 15 C1/C2L/C2R conditions plus the degree-one covering homotopy in prose

claims.claim: The five-state edge matrix has spectral radius phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2; log(phi) lies in the closed interval [0.481211825059603,0.481211825059604].
claims.basis: integer characteristic polynomial, positive eigenvector over Q(phi), and a positive-term series evaluated with rational square-root enclosures and a rational tail bound

claims.claim: There exists a compact nonempty Lambda in the union of the five strips with P(Lambda)=Lambda and h_top(P|Lambda)>=log(phi).
claims.basis: C01-C04, external closed-chain covering theorem, compactness and a continuous surjective itinerary map to the one-sided edge shift

claims.claim: Both saved-record checkers agree on all five coverings for the same exact inputs.
claims.basis: paper-stage offline audit; zero new ODE integrations

nonclaims: first rigorous proof of chaos in the spacetime or general qualitative novelty
an exhaustive priority claim, particularly against full-text-unread Pantig 2026

a bound per unit physical or affine time
new physical phenomena or the full black-hole shadow
formal verification in Lean of the ODE, interval software or topological deduction
independent selection of boxes/strips or completely blind original verification
human peer review, author approval or external publication

formalization.state: L0; no Lean-verified theorem or interface
formalization.reason: Executable interval certificates and an external covering theorem currently have no Lean-verified interface.

literature_limits.qualitative_chaos_context: Appendix A is our application of Bolotin-Kozlov Theorem 2.1 to the optical geodesic flow on a compact invariant set. That theorem does not specify the five strips or the numerical entropy bound per return.
